news.title: Flamingos: 5 records Nigeria broke at 2026 U-17 World Cup
news.lede: Published on 9 Nov 2026 at 17:32 by Imhonlamhen. Nigeria’s Flamingos made history on Saturday, November 7, after beating Japan 2-1 in the final of the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Rabat, Morocco. Goals from Awawu Bashiru and Oluebube Umejiaku secured Nigeria’s first title in the competition and made them the first African nation to win the women’s U-17 World Cup. The victory also ended Africa’s wait for a FIFA women’s world title at any level.

news.title: FIFA U-17 World Cup triumph: SKAID Foundation award Flamingos star scholarship
news.lede: November 9, 2026 Austine Agbo Emmanuel Sports 0. The Southern Kaduna Aid Foundation (SKAID) has announced a fully funded university scholarship for Nigeria’s Flamingos forward, Queen Joseph, in recognition of her contribution to the country’s historic victory at the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. The foundation said the scholarship would cover Queen’s education through to graduation at any university of her choice in Nigeria, blueprint reports. Queen, an Atyap daughter from Zango Kataf Local Government Area of Kaduna State, was part of the Nigerian team that defeated Japan 2-1 in the final on November 7 in Rabat, Morocco, to become the first African country to win the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup.

news.title: Europe's top international scorers: Cristiano Ronaldo out in front, ahead of Romelu Lukaku, Robert Lewandowski and Harry Kane | UEFA Nations League
news.lede: Cristiano Ronaldo scored a staggering 146 international goals for Portugal. Who else is among the leading goalscorers? Cristiano Ronaldo retires from duty for Portugal having become the first European to reach 100 international goals in autumn 2020 – and remains well out in front as both Europe's and the world's all-time leading scorer. He marked his 200th Portugal appearance with an 89th-minute winner in Iceland on 20 June 2023 before rubber-stamping his side's place at UEFA EURO 2024 with two goals against Slovakia on 13 October 2023.

news.title: Argentina youth international Kiki Ramos switches allegiance to Haiti for U-17 World Cup
news.lede: Ramos has been touted as the next prodigy from Argentina. Stephen “Kiki” Ramos, a teenage player from Velez Sarsfield, has chosen to represent Haiti on the international front by playing for Haiti instead of Argentina in the FIFA Under-17 World Cup 2026 in Qatar. Ramos was born in Port-au-Prince on April 3, 2009, and after surviving the horrific 2010 Haitian earthquake, he relocated to Argentina as a baby. He was raised in Buenos Aires and established his football career at Velez Sarsfield after being adopted by an Argentine family.

news.title: Peter Obi Claims NFF Officials Blocked Him from Greeting Flamingos After World Cup Win
news.lede: NDC presidential candidate, Peter Obi, says he will serve for only one term of four years if elected President in 2027. The Nigeria Democratic Congress presidential candidate Peter Obi has alleged that officials of the Nigeria Football Federation prevented him from greeting members of the national Under-17 women’s football team, the Flamingos, following their historic victory at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. Obi said he was allegedly informed that the officials had warned against allowing him to approach the players, allegedly threatening that they would lose their jobs if he did.

news.title: Haiti-born soccer prodigy Kiki Ramos joins Grenadiers ahead of youth World Cup
news.lede: The Haitian Football Federation confirmed Sunday that Haiti-born forward Kiki Ramos, who made headlines for his talent while playing for Argentina this summer, agreed to join the Under-17 Grenadiers’ World Cup training camp in Brazil. Primary Category: Haiti News. Stephen Oscar “Kiki” Ramos, a Haiti-born forward who made his debut for Argentina’s under-17 national team in July, has switched his allegiance to Les Petits Grenadiers. The teenage soccer sensation has joined Haiti’s training camp in Brazil as the team prepares for the FIFA U-17 World Cup in Qatar this fall.

news.title: History Makers! Flamingos Return to Abuja With Historic World Cup Trophy
news.lede: The young champions landed at the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport in the early hours of Monday, November 9, bringing home the trophy after defeating Japan 2-1 in Saturday’s final in Rabat. Officials of the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) and supporters welcomed the team on arrival as celebrations began to honour their remarkable achievement. The victory marked Nigeria’s first-ever title in the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup, making the country the first African nation to win the competition. It also represents a major breakthrough for African women’s football, as no African women’s national team had previously won a FIFA World Cup title at any level.

news.title: Kiki Ramos chooses Haiti over Argentina for Under-17 World Cup
news.lede: Velez Sarsfield youngster Stephen “Kiki” Ramos has decided to represent Haiti rather than Argentina at the upcoming FIFA Under-17 World Cup in Qatar, choosing to honour his birthplace on the international stage. Born on April 3, 2009, in Port-au-Prince, Ramos moved to Argentina as an infant after surviving the devastating 2010 Haiti earthquake. He was adopted by an Argentine family and grew up in Buenos Aires, where he developed his football career at Velez Sarsfield. The talented winger had previously represented Argentina’s Under-17 side in friendly matches.
